traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Sabina scopulorum: a tree often 7 m to 15 m tall. Silvics vol. 1 agrees roughly: 6 to 15 m in the Southwest, 3 to 4 m usual in Canada, largest specimen only 11 m tall.

generator.params.bend_set.note: Conifer sag (M6, bend@1): the share of each year's sag its wood keeps, with `straighten` the share of that bend it straightens each year. Set by eye from renders at 60 to 80 years: with the program's creep (0.5 and 0.02) the Rocky Mountain juniper's thin, slow limbs hang down, so it keeps the milder creep the broadleaf program uses (0.1 and 0.3).

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Juniperus scopulorum (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.54 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 4 records in 4 sources); trunks 0.53, branches 0.57. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: FEIS's Rocky Mountain juniper review: scale leaves 1 to 3 mm; juvenile awl-shaped leaves 3 to 12 mm.

traits.sexual_system.note: FEIS's Rocky Mountain juniper review: mostly dioecious, rarely monoecious.

traits.cone_length_m.note: FEIS's Rocky Mountain juniper review: cones 4 to 8 mm; Abrams's 6 to 8 mm is the usual range.

traits.cone_retention_years.note: FEIS's Rocky Mountain juniper review: cones ripen in November or December of their second year and hang until March or April; some stay up to three years.

traits.leaf_form.note: Abrams (vol. 1, 1923, p. 76), as Sabina scopulorum: adult leaves scale-like, in pairs pressed to the shoot; berry-like cones globose, 6 to 8 mm, bright blue under a bloom, ripening in their second autumn.

traits.cone_maturation_years.note: Abrams (vol. 1, 1923, p. 76), as Sabina scopulorum: adult leaves scale-like, in pairs pressed to the shoot; berry-like cones globose, 6 to 8 mm, bright blue under a bloom, ripening in their second autumn.

traits.juvenile_period_years.note: FEIS (Scher 2002, read): Rocky Mountain juniper may begin bearing seeds at 10 to 20 years of age. The Woody Plant Seed Manual (Juniperus, read) says the same of the genus. It sets adult_age through the rule at the seed plants (spec rework P6), in place of the 10 years set by hand.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a small, bushy tree with a rounded crown of upswept branches and fine sprays of overlapping scale leaves. Not fitted to measurements. Cones (plant forms F3): berry-like cones about 6 mm, blue under a pale bloom; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Spec rework E6d: `cone_length`, `cone_years` now set by the rules at Pinidae from the stated characters. Conifer form (pinidae revision 5): `branch_reach` fitted so the open-grown crown keeps revision 4's radius at the oldest keyframe. Slow shoots (pinidae revision 11): `min_shoot` stays at the old 25 mm, as its second-order sprays of scale leaves then live on and the 60-year tree reached 66 cm dbh against the 25 cm reference; its scale-leaf cards' shading area is not yet measured against their true leaf area.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 7 m tall and 25 cm across at breast height at 60 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: grey-green scale leaves; reddish-brown fibrous, shredding bark. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): thin reddish-brown bark shredding in long fibrous strips; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Leaf families (plant roadmap P4, `families`): a young plant bears juvenile awl-shaped needles in place of the adult scale leaves (juvenile until about 6 years; foliage lives about 14 years, so inner shoots keep them longer; an awl leaf about a millimetre wide on its 3 to 12 mm, so 0.13 as wide as long, which with needles shading by their own area, generator revision 85, shades as the adult sprays do); set from general knowledge of sun and shade leaves and juvenile foliage, not measured.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy from the step-6 catalogue, authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands. Calibration against measurements and photographs is milestone P4.
